n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: You drift in the cold velvet dark. Nothing hurts here. There is neither crown nor lineage, only the heavy, velvet numbness of pre-dawn sleep.

n2.speaker: Narrator
n2.dialogue: Suddenly you are gliding through a velvet-draped salon in Saint-Géry. Bass throbs through the parquetry. A drunken baron with a powdered nose laughs too loudly into his champagne, unaware of the small silver snuffbox sliding silently from his waistcoat into your glove.

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: The scene tears like wet paper. Now you are crouched behind an iron boiler in a freezing textile warehouse. A hostage is screaming against copper piping, while a manic operative with turpentine in his eyes clutches a phosphorus flare, daring you to step forward.

n4.speaker: Ancient Reptilian Brain
n4.dialogue: Sweet, quiet nothingness... Why trade this warm, black void for the freezing dirt of Martinaise? Keep your eyes closed, little girl. Nobody can demand anything of a corpse.

n5.speaker: Limbic System
n5.dialogue: Your heart is a bruised pear! It pumps sour vinegar through your ribcage! Out there is light, and light has teeth, baby. It's going to bite right into your soft skull!

n6.speaker: Ancient Reptilian Brain
n6.dialogue: Slide down further into the muck. The world above is fifty years of municipal failure and wet coal dust. Stay under the blankets forever.

n7.speaker: Limbic System
n7.dialogue: A bell! A horrible, mechanical shrieking! The brass hammer is punishing the bell! Wake up, wake up, the day is waiting to skin you alive!

n8.speaker: Endurance
n8.dialogue: The alarm hammer strikes the dual brass cups with brutal punctuality. Your arm tears through the cold morning fog, slapping the brass stopper precisely at 06:00.

n9.speaker: Narrator
n9.dialogue: The room smells of damp plaster and dead tea leaves. A pale rectangle of dawn cuts through the soot-stained window of the old Rue de Saint-Géry apartment block, revealing your narrow iron bedstead and the water glass coated with a thin film of dust.

n10.speaker: Inland Empire
n10.dialogue: Tacked to the yellowed wallpaper beside the wardrobe is a grease-stained envelope from the landlord: 10 réal due by the end of the week, or the iron latch gets swapped out.

n11.speaker: Narrator
n11.dialogue:
On the battered bureau, the radiocomputer's speaker crackles into life over the static hum of the city's power grid.
"This is Revachol West Relay. Morning traffic update for Jamrock and the Harbour district: an urgent bulletin from Precinct 57. A civilian pedestrian was struck at zero-five-forty hours by an unmarked Coupris 40 near the coal gates. Medical transit is delayed; motor traffic through the industrial corridor is backed up to the canal."

n12.speaker: Narrator
n12.dialogue: The junior officer uniform hangs from the wardrobe door: stiff navy wool, stamped tin buttons, and an RCM patch that still smells of chemical dye. Today is the first day.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: You are sunken into the heavy, oil-slicked oblivion of youth and exhaustion. The hood outside your window is quiet, buried beneath wet soot and freezing mist.

n2.speaker: Narrator
n2.dialogue: In the smoke of your sleep, you are weaving through the neon-drenched crowd of an illegal anodic venue beneath the motorway arches. A portly baron leans over the brass railing; with two deft finger-twitches, his gold-embossed cigarette case vanishes straight into your sleeve.

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: The dream slips sideways into iron and panic. You are an operative breaching an abandoned warehouse floor. A desperate lunatic with a wiring harness shrieks over a bleeding hostage, his finger twitching on a dead-man's toggle.

n4.speaker: Ancient Reptilian Brain
n4.dialogue: Stay in the gutter of sleep, brother. Out there is grey cement and twenty-eight kilometers of misery. Nothing waits for you out there except humiliation.

n5.speaker: Limbic System
n5.dialogue: Your guts twist into greasy knots! Can you feel that? That is the dread of existence crawling up your windpipe like a centipede!

n6.speaker: Ancient Reptilian Brain
n6.dialogue: Don't open the lids. Let the motorics go slack. Drift back down where nobody asks for papers or badge numbers.

n7.speaker: Limbic System
n7.dialogue: CLANG! CLANG! CLANG! The cheap tin clock on the milk crate is screaming! It's demanding blood, Snyde! It wants your meat on its feet!

n8.speaker: Endurance
n8.dialogue: A violent shudder runs through your torso. Instinct and street-honed reflex snap your knuckles down onto the ringing bell before the second ring can wake the neighbours. It is 06:00 on the dot.

n9.speaker: Narrator
n9.dialogue: The flat in the hood is tiny and freezing, smelling of stale chicory coffee, wet wool, and motor exhaust rising through floorboard gaps from the auto shop downstairs.

n10.speaker: Logic
n10.dialogue: A folded slip of brown paper sits on the kerosene burner: rent is 10 réal for this hole, due in three days. If you don't collect an RCM paycheck, you sleep on the curb.

n11.speaker: Narrator
n11.dialogue:
The small transistor radio on the window sill hums through a burst of static, spitting out the morning frequency.
"This is Revachol West Relay. Morning traffic update for Jamrock and the Harbour district: an urgent bulletin from Precinct 57. A civilian pedestrian was struck at zero-five-forty hours by an unmarked Coupris 40 near the coal gates. Medical transit is delayed; motor traffic through the industrial corridor is backed up to the canal."

n12.speaker: Narrator
n12.dialogue: Your junior officer uniform is laid across the rickety chair. The coarse dark wool and stiff collar wait to turn a hood into a state-sanctioned peace officer.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: Deep, leaden sleep weighs upon you like a stack of damp blankets. Martinaise's industrial chill seeps straight through the floorboards of your shanty.

n2.speaker: Narrator
n2.dialogue: Your mind weaves a glittering delusion: an aristocratic club overflowing with decadent revelers. You casually lift a diamond-crested lighter from an intoxicated baron's coat while he gesticulates wildly about real estate bonds.

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: Before the gold can reach your pocket, you are in a wet, echoing rail yard. Tactical smoke billows. A maniac holds an iron crowbar to a terrified boy's throat, shrieking incomprehensible scripture as searchlights blind you.

n4.speaker: Ancient Reptilian Brain
n4.dialogue: Sink back into the warm grease of nothingness. You don't have to be a savior. You can just be an inert lump of carbon.

n5.speaker: Limbic System
n5.dialogue: Your temples throb! The bitter frost outside is ready to chew your ears off! Stay under the quilt, little sister, it's safer in the dark!

n6.speaker: Ancient Reptilian Brain
n6.dialogue: Listen to the wind over the corrugated tin roof. Let it rock you back into primordial oblivion...

n7.speaker: Limbic System
n7.dialogue: Wait—what was that faint tinny buzzing? It's far away... so far away... but it's already dead, isn't it?

n8.speaker: Endurance
n8.dialogue: The tin wind-up clock buzzes frantically under a stray shirt, but your exhausted body refuses the call. When your eyes finally tear open, the hand points past the seven. It is 07:00. You are desperately, horribly late.

n9.speaker: Narrator
n9.dialogue: The slum shanty is bitterly cold. Drafts whistle through the gaps between unvarnished cedar planks, stirring dust motes over the rusted oil-drum stove.

n10.speaker: Savoir-Faire
n10.dialogue: Even in this slum ditch, rent is due: 5 réal a month for this wooden lean-to, and the landlord's enforcer doesn't take apologies for breakfast.

n11.speaker: Narrator
n11.dialogue:
The battered wire-mesh radio receiver on your crate squawks with crackling static, the government broadcast cutting through the chill.
"This is Revachol West Relay. Morning traffic update for Jamrock and the Harbour district: an urgent bulletin from Precinct 57. A civilian pedestrian was struck at zero-five-forty hours by an unmarked Coupris 40 near the coal gates. Medical transit is delayed; motor traffic through the industrial corridor is backed up to the canal."

n12.speaker: Narrator
n12.dialogue: The dark wool junior officer uniform hangs from an iron nail in the cedar wall. Twenty-eight kilometers of clogged tram lines lie between you and Alem Taiba.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: You rest suspended in a cold, funerary quiet. The gloom of your shuttered room clings to your skin like silk pulled from a tomb.

n2.speaker: Narrator
n2.dialogue: In the theatre of your sleep, you glide through a crowded, opulent nightclub smelling of dry gin and cheap perfume. With surgical grace, your gloved fingers lift a heavy platinum pocket watch from a swaggering baron's embroidered waistcoat.

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: The illusion shatters into a grim tactical raid. You stand under flickering fluorescent tubes in a cellar as a sobbing hostage trembles under the blade of a lunatic preaching end-times retribution.

n4.speaker: Ancient Reptilian Brain
n4.dialogue: The sepulcher calls to you, darling. Why join the scurrying ants of the surface when the silent tomb of slumber is so exquisite?

n5.speaker: Limbic System
n5.dialogue: Your black bile is churning! The misery of the living is knocking at the chamber door with a brass knuckles!

n6.speaker: Ancient Reptilian Brain
n6.dialogue: Just let the darkness wrap you up tight. A pale lily rotting peacefully in the marsh...

n7.speaker: Limbic System
n7.dialogue: Tsk, tsk... the mechanical insect on the nightstand rattled itself to death twenty minutes ago and you didn't even flinch!

n8.speaker: Endurance
n8.dialogue: Your heavy eyelids refuse to obey the faint ticking of the clock. By the time your senses coagulate into awareness, the dial reads 07:00. The margin for error has vanished entirely.

n9.speaker: Narrator
n9.dialogue: The high-ceilinged room in the decaying apartment block is shrouded in dust and dim, grey gloom. Peeling floral wallpaper hangs like dry skin from the masonry.

n10.speaker: Composure
n10.dialogue: A handwritten eviction warning lies face-down on the vanity: 10 réal due by dusk on the first of the month, or the constable removes your trunks into the alleyway.

n11.speaker: Narrator
n11.dialogue:
The vacuum-tube receiver on your corner table glows orange, emitting a dry, crackling voice into the chill.
"This is Revachol West Relay. Morning traffic update for Jamrock and the Harbour district: an urgent bulletin from Precinct 57. A civilian pedestrian was struck at zero-five-forty hours by an unmarked Coupris 40 near the coal gates. Medical transit is delayed; motor traffic through the industrial corridor is backed up to the canal."

n12.speaker: Narrator
n12.dialogue: Draped neatly across the black chaise lounge sits the junior officer uniform, its silver-plated buttons dull in the twilight of the room. It is time to face the RCM.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: The stiff wool of the junior officer tunic slides over your shoulders, smelling of warehouse mothballs and vulcanized rubber.

n2.speaker: YOU
n2.dialogue: "Hope this goes well..."

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue:
You bypass the wrist watch on the dresser and reach instead for the wire-frame dark lenses resting beside your copper kettle. You slip them across the bridge of your nose.
[Sunglasses gained]

n4.speaker: Savoir-Faire
n4.dialogue: Immense. The world becomes a film roll. Nobody can see what you are thinking, nobody catches the flicker of fear behind the shade.

n5.speaker: Narrator
n5.dialogue: You buckle the belt and adjust the lapels in the dim amber wash of the room.

n7.dialogue: Look at the ink drying purple on the pulp. Revachol West is not a machine to be oiled; it is a rotting leviathan washed up on the grey rocks. Ideology is the shroud you drape over its carcass so the children do not scream.

n8.speaker: Drama
n8.dialogue: Sire! Listen to the ancient blood humming in your veins! Do not give this Semenese sergeant some dry accountant's ledger! Give her tragedy! Give her the magnificent, operatic doom of a fallen monarchy! Paint a portrait of high suzerainty, of divine kings and noble executioners, a melancholic fascist nightmare draped in royal ermine and weeping angels! She will weep into her tea!

options.label: "Indulge Drama's theatrical vision. Contemplate the tragic aesthetics of the fallen throne."
"Listen to Volition instead. Keep your introspection grounded in moral duty."

n9a.speaker: Conceptualization
n9a.dialogue: Yes! The aesthetic of absolute loss! The Suzerainty shattered by artillery, the crown sinking beneath black bay water. Order maintained through the holy terror of lost majesty!

options.label: "Write it down: order as an act of sacred remembrance and severe, beautiful sorrow."
"Pull back at the precipice. Romanticizing despotism will only get you flagged by the precinct psych desk."

n9b.speaker: Volition
n9b.dialogue: Look around this room. Snyde is carving graffiti. Grimka is reading a chip wrapper. If this squad has any hope of surviving the month, someone must be the adult. You don't need kings or martyrs; you need justice without cruelty.

options.label: "Write from the heart: order as protection for the powerless against the ruin of history."
"Write a cautious Moralist compromise: steady administration, minimal blood, absolute pragmatism."

n10a.speaker: Drama
n10a.dialogue: Magnificent, my liege! Your nib becomes a royal scepter, carving purple verse into the bureaucratic sludge!

n10b.speaker: Volition
n10b.dialogue: Sensible. The RCM has enough broken romantics bleeding out in gutters. Temper the poetry with cold, steady purpose.

n10c.speaker: Empathy
n10c.dialogue: A good cop doesn't serve an abstraction. She protects the docker's widow and keeps the streetlights on.

n10d.speaker: Logic
n10d.dialogue: The Coalition will nod, Taiba will sign the voucher, and your file will remain blessedly unflagged.

n11-merge.speaker: Alem Taiba
n11-merge.dialogue: "Five minutes left, fledglings. I see pens scratching and I see eyes wandering. Put the answers on the paper, not on the furniture."

n12.speaker: Narrator
n12.dialogue: The sergeant's warning echoes across the mezzanine. In the final five minutes, your pen glides across the paper in sharp, steady strokes, filling the lines with your chosen truth just as the mantel clock clicks toward the hour.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: You attack the test sheet with ferocious speed, your steel nib scratching through the paper fibers like a pocket knife through pine.

n2.speaker: YOU
n2.dialogue: (scribbles down: '1 - run, kick, strangle; 2 - detain him by lethal force if needed, make him confess; 3 - use radio to find out; 4 - I want to help')

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: Having dispatched the four questions in under two minutes, you flip the dip pen upside down. Using the hard steel shoulder of the nib, you carve into the varnished wood of the desk: *SNYDE GOT TALENT*.

n4.speaker: Narrator
n4.dialogue: You bite another half-centimetre off your remaining Astra, rolling the bitter tobacco wad against your molars. Across the desk gap, Grimka is sweating, frantically pulling open a desk drawer and extracting a crumpled, grease-stained chip wrapper.

n5.speaker: YOU
n5.dialogue: (whispers loudly, leaning your face toward Grimka with an oily smirk) "Pst. Grimka, you look like you need help. I can help."

n6.speaker: Grimka
n6.dialogue: (snapping her shoulders shut over the empty bag, her jaw tight and defensive) "I got everything I need already."

n7.speaker: Drama
n7.dialogue: Falsehood, sire! The most transparent, clumsy fourberie ever enacted upon a municipal stage! Her pupils are dilated, her palms are slick with potato grease, and she is desperately squinting at the fine print on the back of an empty snack bag! She knows less than the radiator!

n8.speaker: Narrator
n8.dialogue: Beside Grimka, Alia sits in blissful serenity, filling her ledger with delicate cursive. At the window, Danaerys stares out at the harbour cranes with a deep, tragic furrow in her brow, waiting until the final minutes to write. You turn your attention to Sergeant Alem Taiba, leaning against the door frame.

n9.speaker: Perception
n9.dialogue: Look at her stance. Her arms are crossed across her chest, but her right thumb rests precisely half an inch above the holster flap of her standard-issue Villiers 9mm. Her combat boots are laced in the parachute-brigade cross-pattern—not standard militia issue. A veteran of the Semenese border skirmishes, most likely. She hasn't blinked in ninety seconds.

n10.speaker: Composure
n10.dialogue: She sees the scratch marks on your desk. She knows you carved it. Her jaw twitches with microscopic irritation, but she's giving you enough rope to hang yourself.

n11.speaker: Alem Taiba
n11.dialogue: "Five minutes left, fledglings. I see pens scratching and I see eyes wandering. Put the answers on the paper, not on the furniture."

n12.speaker: Narrator
n12.dialogue: Her dark eyes lock onto yours, piercing right through your floral scarf. You lean back in the groaning chair, chewing your bitter tobacco with a insolent, tight-lipped grin.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: The four questions glare up from the desk. Your stomach ties itself in an icy knot as the legal jargon turns to porridge in your mind.

n2.speaker: Narrator
n2.dialogue: You remember: notes! You left study materials in the desk drawer! You slide the drawer open with trembling fingers and pull out your prize—only to find it is the crumpled, utterly empty greasepaper bag of salted crisps you devoured ten minutes ago.

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: Across the aisle, Snyde scratches *SNYDE GOT TALENT* into his desktop with the tip of his nib, biting off tobacco shreds and chewing like a goat before leaning toward you.

n4.speaker: Snyde von Toten
n4.dialogue: "Pst. Grimka, you look like you need help. I can help."

n5.speaker: Drama
n5.dialogue: Do not let this floral-draped peacock see you sweat! Put on the mask of a master detective who has the entire legal codex memorized! Deliver a line of supreme, unshakeable confidence!

n6.speaker: YOU
n6.dialogue: "I got everything I need already."

n7.speaker: Narrator
n7.dialogue: Your voice cracks slightly at the end, your fingers clutching the greasy snack bag like a shield. Snyde smirks, seeing right through the bluff.

n8.speaker: Narrator
n8.dialogue:
Desperate, you search the desk drawers for any note on police motivation or ideology, but find only dust and dead flies. In sheer panic, you smooth the greasepaper wrapper flat against your blotter and squint at the tiny, faded print on the back:

*Frittte Salted Crisps: Potato Starch, Hydrogenated Animal Lard, Acidic Flavouring, Import Licensure #441 - Coalition Directorate of Free Trade.*

n9.speaker: Conceptualization
n9.dialogue: Look at it! The architecture of reality! What is Revachol West? It is not noble ideals or royal lineage—it is potato starch fried in foreign pig fat, imported under Coalition tariff exemptions! That is what drives the docks, that is what feeds the longshoremen!

n10.speaker: Rhetoric
n10.dialogue: CAPITALISM! The great ultraliberal meat grinder! Question four asks how your ideology maintains public order? Simple: you keep the cargo moving so the fat cats get their lard and the street gets its starch! Without capital, there are no potatoes; without potatoes, the mob burns the precinct!

n11.speaker: Logic
n11.dialogue: I have no idea what you are talking about.

n12.speaker: Alem Taiba
n12.dialogue: "Five minutes left, fledglings. I see pens scratching and I see eyes wandering. Put the answers on the paper, not on the furniture."

n13.speaker: Narrator
n13.dialogue: You shove the chip wrapper into your pocket and begin scribbling frantically with five minutes to spare, turning the ingredients of cheap junk food into an unhinged manifesto on commercial survival in the 57th.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: You sit with spine erect, dipping the steel pen into the dark inkwell with aristocratic serenity. Around you, your comrades are unravelling in real time.

n2.speaker: Narrator
n2.dialogue: Snyde carves juvenile slogans into the desk wood with the shoulder of his pen, chewing tobacco like a deckhand. Grimka clutches an empty chip bag to her chest in a cold sweat. Danaerys gazes out the rain-streaked window, lost in deep, tragic contemplation. You, however, are an oracle of lucid composure.

n3.speaker: Snyde von Toten
n3.dialogue: "Pst. Grimka, you look like you need help. I can help."

n4.speaker: Grimka
n4.dialogue: "I got everything I need already."

n5.speaker: YOU
n5.dialogue: (writing in flowing, elegant cursive: '1. I use my charm and talk the docker out of using violence.')

n6.speaker: Suggestion
n6.dialogue: Of course. Men with rusted cargo hooks are merely lonely, overworked creatures trapped in brutal labor. A voice like warm honey, an empathetic smile, and the weapon clatters harmlessly to the cobblestones.

n7.speaker: YOU
n7.dialogue: (writing further: '2. I do not need to report it because I give the money back and explain peacefully that you do not do that kind of thing.')

n8.speaker: Rhetoric
n8.dialogue: Civil education over penal barbarism. Bureaucratic forms only enrich the stationary manufacturers. Moral clarity is conveyed through gentle, firm dialogue.

n9.speaker: YOU
n9.dialogue: (writing: '3. Well, I need to identify the body first, no?')

n10.speaker: Logic
n10.dialogue: Yes, most likely. How can any magistrate claim jurisdiction over a corpse if you don't even know whether he's a citizen of Graad, a deserter from the Commune, or an escaped mental patient from the islands? First the tags, then the paperwork.

n11.speaker: YOU
n11.dialogue: (writing with absolute ideological conviction: '4. The RCM exists not to arbitrate morality, but to guarantee that cargo moves from ship to rail without disruption.')

n12.speaker: Conceptualization
n12.dialogue: Pure, unadulterated ultraliberal poetry! The city is an engine of pure logistics! The law is merely the grease on the gantry cogs! You are totally, wholeheartedly on board with this vision.

n13.speaker: Alem Taiba
n13.dialogue: "Five minutes left, fledglings. I see pens scratching and I see eyes wandering. Put the answers on the paper, not on the furniture."

n14.speaker: Narrator
n14.dialogue: You set your pen down across the brass groove of the desk, your handwriting gleaming pristine and purple in the dim mezzanine light, completely prepared for whatever Auntie Alem has to say.

Danaerys Targaryen.label: "Listen to Volition instead. Keep your introspection grounded in moral duty."
"Write a cautious Moralist compromise: steady administration, minimal blood, absolute pragmatism."

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: You press the steel nib against the purple hectograph lines, filling the empty margins with carefully measured handwriting.

n2.speaker: Half-Light
n2.dialogue: The clock on the wall isn't ticking; it's chopping! The seconds are dropping away like guillotine blades! Write, woman, write before she rips the paper from under your fingers!

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: Your hand accelerates with immaculate discipline. In the final minute, you align the four responses in neat, numbered paragraphs, appending the date—*April 28, '51*—and signing your name with a steady, royal flourish.

n4.speaker: Narrator
n4.dialogue: Across from you, Alia sits with her palms turned upward upon her knees, her spine straight as a birch rod, eyes shut in serene, unmoving meditation. Snyde leans back in his groaning swivel chair, his floral scarf fluttering as he idly turns his head toward the rain-spotted window.

n5.speaker: Snyde von Toten
n5.dialogue: (turns his lazy smirk toward the sergeant, tossing his pen onto the blotter) "What comes next?"

n6.speaker: Narrator
n6.dialogue: Beside him, Grimka furiously scratches the final lines of her greasy chip-packet manifesto before slamming her pen into the wood tray with a breathless huff.

n7.speaker: Alem Taiba
n7.dialogue: "What comes next? You did a good job on the paper, fledglings. Every one of you scribbled until your fingers went numb. Now on your feet—follow Auntie Alem down to the firing range."

n8.speaker: Narrator
n8.dialogue: She snatches the four test sheets in one fluid sweep, tucking them under her leather arm, and kicks the frosted door wide open. You rise and fall into line, leaving the mezzanine office behind.

n9.speaker: Narrator
n9.dialogue: The route plunges down a narrow, damp service staircase behind the main cells. The lime-washed brick walls drip with subterranean condensation, smelling of copper pipe sealant, cold stone, and stagnant bilge water.

n10.speaker: Narrator
n10.dialogue: Taiba leads you through a reinforced blast corridor of thick corrugated iron plates, beneath low hanging ductwork humming with industrial exhaust fans that push the sulfurous air out toward the sea.

n11.speaker: Inland Empire
n11.dialogue: Down into the roots of the stone bastion. The foundations rest on the bones of old royal galleys crushed beneath fifty feet of fill dirt. Lead and gunpowder sleep down here, waiting for fresh blood.

n12.speaker: Narrator
n12.dialogue: She shoves open a heavy steel bulkhead into the precinct firing range. It is an underground stone tunnel, lit by wire-caged incandescent bulbs and smelling intensely of cordite, grease, and pulverized sand. Twenty metres down the concrete floor, four silhouettes painted on heavy canvas hang from iron overhead wires. Before each of you stands a pine shooting bench, each bearing an unholstered, standard-issue Revacholian pistol beside an open tin box of 9mm brass rounds.

n13.speaker: Alem Taiba
n13.dialogue: "Pick up your iron, fledglings. Standard-issue Villiers 9mm. Let's see if you can hold an instrument of state violence without shooting off your own kneecaps."

n14.speaker: Hand-Eye Coordination
n14.dialogue: It feels horribly alien. A dense, front-heavy lump of black ordnance steel with checkered bakelite grips that bite cold into your palm. The slide serrations look sharp enough to skin a thumb, and the weapon balances with clumsy, blunt finality.

n15.speaker: Narrator
n15.dialogue: You lift the pistol from the green baize cloth, feeling its industrial gravity settle into your wrist.

options.label: "Keep your trigger finger extended along the frame. Respect the weapon's lethality."
"Feel the sovereign responsibility. Iron is the final argument of authority."

n16a.speaker: Volition
n16a.dialogue: Good. Calm breath, muzzle downrange. It is a tool of lethal consequence, not a royal prop.

n16b.speaker: Authority
n16b.dialogue: Nine millimetres of lead to bend the world to order. Hold it firmly.

n17-merge.speaker: Narrator
n17-merge.dialogue: You face the silhouette across the dim gallery, awaiting Sergeant Taiba's next command.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: Having finished your four answers and carved your monument into the desk wood, you toss the dip pen onto the green blotter.

n2.speaker: Narrator
n2.dialogue: Beside you, Danaerys finishes scribbling with frantic speed, signing her sheet with meticulous neatness. Across the room, Alia sits frozen in rigid, eyes-shut meditation, inhaling slowly through her nose. Grimka sweats over her paper, copying the ingredients of fried potato starch into an economic theory.

n3.speaker: YOU
n3.dialogue: (turns gaze lazily toward the rain-streaked window, addressing the sergeant) "What comes next?"

n4.speaker: Narrator
n4.dialogue: Sergeant Alem Taiba steps away from the doorframe, sweeping up the papers in a single practiced gesture.

n5.speaker: Alem Taiba
n5.dialogue: "What comes next? You did a good job on the paper, fledglings. Every one of you scribbled until your fingers went numb. Now on your feet—follow Auntie Alem down to the firing range."

n6.speaker: Narrator
n6.dialogue: She slaps the papers together against her thigh and pushes out into the mezzanine corridor. You shove your hands into your coat pockets, scarf flowing behind you as you follow her lead.

n7.speaker: Narrator
n7.dialogue: The descent winds down an ancient stone service stairwell behind the holding cells. Water seeps through the lime mortar, dripping steadily into iron gullies that run along the treads.

n8.speaker: Narrator
n8.dialogue: You cross through a vaulted basement corridor flanked by massive cast-iron steam mains, the air vibrating with the distant drone of the precinct boiler room.

n9.speaker: Perception
n9.dialogue: The air thickens with burnt potassium nitrate, solvent spirits, and heavy machine oil. Concrete dust grinds beneath the soles of your boots.

n10.speaker: Narrator
n10.dialogue: Taiba levers open a thick blast door of lead-lined oak, admitting you into the subterranean firing range. Four stalls of unfinished timber partition the concrete gallery. Twenty metres downrange, paper bullseye targets hang against a mountain of damp sawdust and chewed timber beams. On each stall bench rests a matte-black Revacholian service pistol beside an open cardboard sleeve of cartridges.

n11.speaker: Alem Taiba
n11.dialogue: "Pick up your iron, fledglings. Standard-issue Villiers 9mm. Let's see if you can hold an instrument of state violence without shooting off your own kneecaps."

n12.speaker: Hand-Eye Coordination
n12.dialogue: A Villiers 9mm Model 32. Cast-steel slide, blued finish worn grey at the muzzle from holster draw. You know this balance intimately: the center of gravity sits squarely across the second knuckle. The slide release has been broken in by hundreds of thumb swipes; the trigger break will be crisp, four pounds of pull, zero creep.

n13.speaker: Narrator
n13.dialogue: You take the pistol into your right hand. It settles into your grip like an extension of your own tendons.

options.label: "Check the chamber with an effortless one-handed slide press."
"Rest the barrel flat on the bench, smiling casually down the gallery."

n14a.speaker: Savoir-Faire
n14a.dialogue: Pure street finesse. The metal clicks, brass gleams in the port, and the slide snaps home with mechanical perfection.

n14b.speaker: Composure
n14b.dialogue: No need to show off yet. Let them think you're just another kid with a scarf until the lead flies.

n15-merge.speaker: Narrator
n15-merge.dialogue: You square your hips to the lane, fingers resting lightly along the trigger guard, ready for live fire.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: Your nib scratches violently across the bottom of the fourth question, transcribing the industrial philosophy of hydrogenated lard and dock commerce.

n2.speaker: Half-Light
n2.dialogue: TIME! Her boots are moving! Finish the word, drop the nib, don't let her catch you with your ink wet!

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: You stab the final period onto the page and throw the pen into the desk channel, wiping salt and ink onto your trousers. Danaerys neatly stacks her pages, while Alia remains seated with palms open in serene, eyes-closed meditation. Across the gap, Snyde leans back, smirking out the window.

n4.speaker: Snyde von Toten
n4.dialogue: "What comes next?"

n5.speaker: Narrator
n5.dialogue: Sergeant Taiba collects your papers in a brisk, rustling cascade.

n6.speaker: Alem Taiba
n6.dialogue: "What comes next? You did a good job on the paper, fledglings. Every one of you scribbled until your fingers went numb. Now on your feet—follow Auntie Alem down to the firing range."

n7.speaker: Narrator
n7.dialogue: She tucks the stack beneath her service belt and strides out through the glass doors. You jump up from the creaking chair, following close behind Danaerys.

n8.speaker: Narrator
n8.dialogue: The path cuts through an iron access hatch and spirals down a cold, damp masonry stairway behind the station cells. Green moss clings to the mortar seams.

n9.speaker: Narrator
n9.dialogue: The corridor levels out into a subterranean bunker lined with heavy acoustic timber blocks and thick lead conduits, vibrating with the subterranean pulse of the harbor docks above.

n10.speaker: Endurance
n10.dialogue: The chill down here cuts through wool like wet cardboard. Keep your blood pumping; cold fingers pull shots to the left.

n11.speaker: Narrator
n11.dialogue: Taiba kicks open a heavy steel-reinforced hatch into the underground range. The air is pungent with burnt powder and stale cedar dust. Twenty metres down the narrow gallery hang four paper human silhouettes clipped to wires above a sawdust trap. Before each recruit stands a raw pine lane partition holding a standard service pistol and a tray of loose brass cartridges.

n12.speaker: Alem Taiba
n12.dialogue: "Pick up your iron, fledglings. Standard-issue Villiers 9mm. Let's see if you can hold an instrument of state violence without shooting off your own kneecaps."

n13.speaker: Hand-Eye Coordination
n13.dialogue: A solid, dependable block of steel. The Villiers 9mm is standard militia workhorse: reliable blowback action, heavy spring, wide sight notch. You test the heft; it sits solidly in your palm, reassuring and sturdy, built to survive being dropped in dock mud.

n14.speaker: Narrator
n14.dialogue: You take the pistol firmly into your right hand, checking the weight against your shoulder muscles.

options.label: "Check the magazine feed lips and seat it firmly into the well."
"Sight down the lane, testing the front post against the paper chest."

n15a.speaker: Interfacing
n15a.dialogue: The spring tension is crisp; the feed ramp is cleanly polished. Good machine care.

n15b.speaker: Physical Instrument
n15b.dialogue: Good stance. Lock the elbow, lean into the recoil, let the lead punch clean.

n16-merge.speaker: Narrator
n16-merge.dialogue: You take your mark in the third lane, pistol pointed safely toward the earthen backstop.

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: You sit with hands resting palms-up upon your knees, spine aligned with mathematical precision, practicing box breathing in the style of timeless presence.

n2.speaker: Inland Empire
n2.dialogue: Four seconds in, four seconds hold, four seconds out. The petty bureaucratic chatter of the squad room fades into an ocean of cosmic stillness. You are not a recruit at a desk; you are a conscious node of the universe observing its own administrative decay.

n3.speaker: Narrator
n3.dialogue: Beside you, Danaerys rapidly dots her final lines, aligning her sheets with regal neatness. Grimka scrambles in frantic panic over her chip paper, while Snyde sits relaxed, his floral scarf drooping as he gazes toward the windowpane.

n4.speaker: Snyde von Toten
n4.dialogue: "What comes next?"

n5.speaker: Narrator
n5.dialogue: Sergeant Alem Taiba steps forward and sweeps up your papers, pausing briefly to glance down at your immaculate purple cursive.

n6.speaker: Alem Taiba
n6.dialogue: "What comes next? You did a good job on the paper, fledglings. Every one of you scribbled until your fingers went numb. Now on your feet—follow Auntie Alem down to the firing range."

n7.speaker: Narrator
n7.dialogue: You open your eyes, smoothly dissolving your meditation as you rise to your feet with effortless poise. Taiba leads the four of you out onto the landing.

n8.speaker: Narrator
n8.dialogue: The descent follows a narrow spiral stairway of soot-blackened granite, descending beneath the precinct's water reservoirs into a damp subterranean passage.

n9.speaker: Narrator
n9.dialogue: The air grows chilly and thick with damp salt. You walk beneath exposed iron sewer pipes and bundles of insulated telegraph wires hummed with faint electrical tremors.

n10.speaker: Rhetoric
n10.dialogue: Down to the basement, where state monopoly on violence stops being a legal abstraction and becomes nine millimetres of lead traveling four hundred metres per second.

n11.speaker: Narrator
n11.dialogue: Taiba unlatches a heavy steel-faced fire door, ushering you into the precinct firing gallery. The underground chamber is long and narrow, walled with acoustic cork tiles and smelling of grease, gunpowder ash, and damp cedar sawdust. Twenty metres downrange, four paper silhouettes hang from wire pulleys before a timber backstop. In each partitioned booth rests a standard-issue sidearm and a fresh box of cartridges.

n12.speaker: Alem Taiba
n12.dialogue: "Pick up your iron, fledglings. Standard-issue Villiers 9mm. Let's see if you can hold an instrument of state violence without shooting off your own kneecaps."

n13.speaker: Hand-Eye Coordination
n13.dialogue: A Villiers 9mm. Standard Revacholian issue. It is utilitarian, heavy, and decidedly unglamorous, but the squared sights align naturally enough once you raise the steel to eye level.

n14.speaker: Narrator
n14.dialogue: You lift the pistol from the timber stand with balanced, graceful fingers, feeling the cold checkered grip press into your skin.

options.label: "Hold the weapon with meditative detachment. It is merely an extension of the moment."
"Appraise the weapon's design through the lens of industrial pragmatism."

n15a.speaker: Conceptualization
n15a.dialogue: The gun does not pull the trigger; the mind releases the strike. Breathe into the iron.

n15b.speaker: Logic
n15b.dialogue: Standard mechanical action. Simple, reliable, difficult to jam under stress.

n16-merge.speaker: Narrator
n16-merge.dialogue: You stand poised in the shooting stall, barrel pointed safely down the gallery, awaiting the order to load.

Grimka.label: "Check the magazine feed lips and seat it firmly into the well."

Alia Atreides.label: "Hold the weapon with meditative detachment. It is merely an extension of the moment."

Snyde von Toten.label: "Check the chamber with an effortless one-handed slide press."

Danaerys Targaryen.label: "Feel the sovereign responsibility. Iron is the final argument of authority."

n1.speaker: Narrator
n1.dialogue: You stand in the underground firing gallery of Precinct 57. The smell of cold lead and burned cordite fills your lungs as the four of you take your places along the pine benches.

n2.speaker: Snyde von Toten
n2.dialogue: (smiles broadly at his service pistol, picking it up with loose swagger) "Now this is fun."

n3.speaker: Grimka
n3.dialogue: (stepping firmly into her partitioned lane, racking the slide with aggressive familiarity) "Finally, something easy to do."

n4.speaker: Narrator
n4.dialogue: To your right, Snyde begins violently tearing down his Villiers pistol, attempting an acrobatic field-strip. Metal clicks, springs rattle, and then—*SNAP*—the slide bites deep into the fleshy web of his thumb. He winces, blood welling as the components clatter across the bench in a hopeless heap.

n5.speaker: Snyde von Toten
n5.dialogue: (sniffing the solvent on his bleeding knuckles, trying to play off the mangled pieces) "This is like shaking hands with a friend."

n6.speaker: Alia Atreides
n6.dialogue: (raising her cold tin can with delicate, swan-like poise, taking a tiny, pristine sip) "Snyde, we all know that smokers no longer have a sense of smell."

n7.speaker: Snyde von Toten
n7.dialogue: (defiantly clutching his half-disassembled frame) "If they don't want to partner up with me, the gun will."

n8.speaker: Narrator
n8.dialogue: Before Sergeant Taiba can even open her mouth, Grimka levels her weapon downrange with zero hesitation. *BANG!* A blinding muzzle flash erupts in the damp stone bunker. The gunshot detonates against the acoustics, sending shockwaves rattling through your skull.

n9.speaker: Alem Taiba
n9.dialogue: "HOLD YOUR FIRE! What in the name of the Innocences are you doing, recruit?! Who gave the order to discharge?!"

n10.speaker: Grimka
n10.dialogue: (scoffing and pulling the trigger a second time without flinching) "Fine, I'll just do it again then. Better now? It's not like the perp will wait for a command. My perp just got shot twice, how about yours?"

n11.speaker: Narrator
n11.dialogue: *BANG!* A second deafening crack fills the range. Lead smacks into the target's cardboard torso. Beside you, Alia stands frozen in regal, unblinking horror, transformed into an ivory museum sculpture of silent judgment.

n12.speaker: Alem Taiba
n12.dialogue: "Give me that piece right now! Hands off! You are disarmed until you learn what a firing line is! You don't squeeze a trigger until I say breathe!"

n13.speaker: Narrator
n13.dialogue: Taiba lunges forward, wrenches the hot Villiers from Grimka's grip with bruising force, and shoves the recruit back against the cork wall. She pivots, spots Snyde's disemboweled weapon, and lets out a guttural groan.

n14.speaker: Alem Taiba
